text:
Alex: quick q — if a customer on Dedicated hits their reserved GPUs, do we let their requests overflow to Hosted automatically, or should we block/queue?
Maria: my vote is: allow overflow but only with explicit opt-in per-tenant. isolation + compliance customers will opt-out.
Sam: opt-in makes sense. also need to downgrade model variant when overflow happens (e.g., fp16 -> int8) to keep latency/cost predictable.
Priya: +1 opt-in. but we need a clear contract: what metrics change, who pays for the hosted run, and how do we surface this in the Console.
Alex: agreed. For Console UX: show an "Overflow policy" toggle on tenant settings and a per-route override. tiny wireframe: "Allow overflow: Off/Hosted fallback/Queue".
Maria: can we add a read-only badge on requests that used overflow? telemetry team needs to attribute tokens.
InfraBot: NOTE: when routing to Hosted we must strip any VPC-only headers. see internal-sec playbook: https://intranet.redwood/internal-sec/headers.md
Sam: implementation idea: routing decision = if (dedicated_capacity_available) -> dedicated; else if (tenant.allows_overflow) -> hosted_variant; else queue/fail. simple pseudo: ```js
if (pool.hasSlots(req)) return routeTo(pool);
if (tenant.overflow === 'hosted') return routeTo(hosted.pickVariant(req));
return error(429, 'dedicated_capacity_exhausted');
```
Priya: we also need to preserve data isolation guarantees for customers paying for dedicated. they should have an option to pay for "hosted execution with isolation" (dedicated encrypted runtime) if they want overflow but no egress. admin-econ needs to weigh pricing.
Maria: question for telemetry — how do we show end-to-end latency split (enqueue time in dedicated queue vs hosted runtime)? DevEx: could we tag spans with routing.cause and routing.path?
DevEx: yep. add tags: routing.path:{dedicated|hosted}, routing.variant:{v1|v1-int8|v1-quant}, routing.cause:{capacity|region-unavailable|manual}. that gives us filtering.
Alex: good. also need alerting: if >1% of tenant X's requests are overflowing for >5m, notify tenant-owner + infra oncall.
Sam: note: region constraint — if tenant pins to eu-west and hosted capacity is only us-east, should we respect region lock? I think overflow must honor region unless tenant allows cross-region.
Priya: absolutely. default: deny cross-region overflow. explicit consent needed for cross-region.
Maria: billing: hosted run tokens billed at hosted rates, but if tenant has reserved dedicated commit we might prorate — Finance to propose. @Priya can you loop them in?
Priya: looping finance. cc @DevEx for billing UX.
InfraBot: Deploybot: routing-v2 feature branch deploy queued (build #6789).
Alex: on rollout UX — start with feature flag per-org. gradual ramp: 0 -> 1% -> 5% -> 100. Metrics dashboard should show overflow rate and variant-change rate per org.
Sam: corner case: what if dedicated uses modelA and hosted only has compatible modelB with different tokenization? need a compatibility layer or reject.
Maria: add model compatibility check to the routing planner. if not compatible, either can't overflow or we fallback to a compatible variant only if tenant opted in.
DevEx: small ask: in API responses include header X-Redwood-Routing: dedicated|hosted and X-Redwood-Variant for observability.
Alex: agreed. make sure the headers are safe to expose (no PII).
Priya: security note: for regulated customers who opt into overflow, require KMS/HSM integration on hosted path. Ops: what's the feasibility?
Sam: doable but higher cost. we'll flag as premium feature.
Maria: next steps: 1) design Console toggle + badge (DevEx) 2) implement routing decision + headers (Eng-platform) 3) telemetry tags + dashboard (Observability) 4) pricing + legal check (Finance/Sales)
Alex: sounds good. I'll create a GH issue with the checklist and link to this thread.
Priya: thanks all. small follow-up: can we prototype a soft-fail mode that queues overflow requests for 30s before failing? helps burst smoothing.
Sam: prototype ok. queue length must be tenant-configurable with sane defaults.
DevEx: FYI will add a small Console note about what "overflow" means for non-engineers.
Alex: thanks — I'll ping when GH issue is up. :thumbsup:
